purpose: Enhanced, concise JSON skill content derived from full SKILL.md files and open PR descriptions.
enhancement_method: Each entry consolidates purpose, safe validation, defender acceptance checks, and false-positive controls. It is a structured enhancement layer for the source skills.
common_assessment_controls: Confirm written authorization, target boundaries, accounts, methods, and time window before testing.
Prefer isolated labs, synthetic data, and reversible actions; make one controlled change per test.
Capture a baseline and independently verify any claimed effect; distinguish observation from inference.
Stop when a test reaches real-user data, external recipients, privileged access, destructive state, or an unapproved system.
Record cleanup and regression criteria so the owner can safely retest.

enhanced_content.purpose: Assess whether an API binds client-controlled fields beyond the action’s intended DTO, and verify persistence through an authorized read-back.
enhanced_content.safe_validation: Use a disposable record and change one low-impact candidate at a time; verify the saved value independently; avoid privilege, ownership, billing, or production-state changes.
enhanced_content.defender_acceptance: Define request-specific DTOs, allowlist nested fields, map explicitly, and test that unauthorized attributes never persist.
enhanced_content.interpretation_check: An echoed request body or success status alone does not establish persistence.

enhanced_content.purpose: Review session lifecycle controls for identifier rotation, cookie scope, and invalidation across login and privilege changes.
enhanced_content.safe_validation: Use only a controlled test account and browser session; compare identifiers before and after login, logout, and role transitions; avoid real credentials or session reuse across users.
enhanced_content.defender_acceptance: Rotate identifiers at authentication and privilege changes, invalidate old identifiers, and set Secure, HttpOnly, and appropriate SameSite/domain/path attributes.
enhanced_content.interpretation_check: Distinguish a stable cookie value from a server-side session identifier; confirm old identifiers are rejected.

enhanced_content.purpose: Assess whether user input can alter email headers, recipients, or message structure in an authorized mail workflow.
enhanced_content.safe_validation: Use a mail sink or controlled mailbox; send one benign marker at a time; do not route messages to third parties or trigger bulk delivery.
enhanced_content.defender_acceptance: Reject CR/LF in header values, use structured recipient APIs, and keep user input in encoded message bodies.
enhanced_content.interpretation_check: A rendered newline in a body is not header injection; verify the raw message structure in the controlled sink.

enhanced_content.purpose: Identify attacker-controlled named elements that shadow expected DOM properties or globals and affect application behavior.
enhanced_content.safe_validation: Use a local fixture or isolated test page; add inert id/name markers and observe property resolution without data collection or external callbacks.
enhanced_content.defender_acceptance: Avoid security decisions based on mutable document properties; sanitize or constrain names and use explicit references and trusted configuration.
enhanced_content.interpretation_check: Confirm the clobbered property reaches a security-relevant sink; a name collision alone may have no impact.

enhanced_content.purpose: Check whether untrusted input changes LDAP filter or bind semantics in an authorized test environment.
enhanced_content.safe_validation: Use test identities and non-destructive boolean probes; keep queries narrow and avoid enumerating real users or extracting directory data.
enhanced_content.defender_acceptance: Use parameterized filter construction or RFC 4515 escaping appropriate to the filter context; apply least-privilege binds and strict input validation.
enhanced_content.interpretation_check: Separate filter injection from DN injection and verify a changed result predicate rather than relying on status codes.

enhanced_content.purpose: Determine whether input can inject response headers, split responses, or corrupt logs in an in-scope application.
enhanced_content.safe_validation: Use a unique inert marker against staging or a local fixture; inspect headers and controlled logs; avoid cache poisoning or cross-user log manipulation.
enhanced_content.defender_acceptance: Reject CR/LF in header fields, use framework header APIs, and encode structured log fields.
enhanced_content.interpretation_check: Encoded input reflected in a body is not header injection; confirm the marker lands in a distinct header or log field.

enhanced_content.purpose: Evaluate path normalization and confinement for file access routes using harmless, known test files.
enhanced_content.safe_validation: Use a disposable lab and a canary file created for the assessment; keep checks read-only; do not read secrets, include files, execute code, or access unrelated system paths.
enhanced_content.defender_acceptance: Canonicalize once, resolve beneath an allowed root, reject traversal after normalization, and avoid user-controlled wrapper or include schemes.
enhanced_content.interpretation_check: A blocked string or error message does not prove confinement; verify the resolved path or controlled canary result.

enhanced_content.purpose: Assess whether untrusted input reaches SSI or ESI processing and can alter server-side fragment behavior.
enhanced_content.safe_validation: Use a local or staging fixture with a harmless marker and controlled fragment endpoint; do not invoke command execution, internal network access, or data disclosure.
enhanced_content.defender_acceptance: Disable SSI execution, restrict SSI to deliberate file types, and enable ESI only for explicitly trusted origin responses.
enhanced_content.interpretation_check: A literal directive in a response may not be processed; establish which component parses it and under what conditions.

enhanced_content.purpose: Check whether input types or query operators alter document-database predicates or authorization decisions.
enhanced_content.safe_validation: Use a seeded test collection and synthetic accounts; test one predicate at a time; avoid broad enumeration, destructive writes, or server-side JavaScript execution.
enhanced_content.defender_acceptance: Construct queries from typed allowlisted fields and operators, disable server-side JavaScript where unnecessary, and enforce authorization independently of query shape.
enhanced_content.interpretation_check: Differentiate parser errors from changed query semantics; verify results only against synthetic records.

enhanced_content.purpose: Evaluate framing protections and whether a harmless framed interaction can mislead a test user.
enhanced_content.safe_validation: Use a dedicated test account and non-sensitive reversible action; record the frame behavior and stop before any real transfer, deletion, publication, or consent action.
enhanced_content.defender_acceptance: Set a restrictive CSP frame-ancestors, retain compatible legacy headers where needed, and test protection across sensitive routes.
enhanced_content.interpretation_check: Framability alone is not impact; assess whether a real user could be induced to perform a meaningful action.

enhanced_content.purpose: Assess whether ciphertext handling leaks distinguishable padding or decryption validity in an isolated cryptographic test.
enhanced_content.safe_validation: Use synthetic ciphertexts and disposable lab keys; compare uniform error behavior at a conservative rate; do not tamper with production tokens or attempt account/role forgery.
enhanced_content.defender_acceptance: Prefer AEAD, authenticate before decrypting, use constant-time validation, and return indistinguishable failures.
enhanced_content.interpretation_check: Timing noise and generic error differences can create false positives; repeat only in a controlled lab with stable baselines.

enhanced_content.purpose: Identify dangling DNS or third-party service references and measure trust exposure without taking control of a live resource.
enhanced_content.safe_validation: Use passive data and provider error signatures first; obtain explicit owner approval before any claim test; do not host content on a resource referenced by another organization.
enhanced_content.defender_acceptance: Remove DNS records before deprovisioning providers, monitor dangling records, and avoid broad cookie/CORS/CSP trust on subdomains.
enhanced_content.interpretation_check: NXDOMAIN or a provider-branded error is a candidate signal, not proof that the resource is safely claimable.

enhanced_content.purpose: Review whether a cross-site request can trigger a state change using a controlled account and harmless action.
enhanced_content.safe_validation: Use a test account and reversible preference or dummy record; verify token, origin, and cookie behavior; do not trigger payments, messaging, or destructive actions.
enhanced_content.defender_acceptance: Bind anti-CSRF tokens to the session, configure SameSite appropriately, validate Origin/Referer where suitable, and keep credentialed CORS narrowly allowlisted.
enhanced_content.interpretation_check: A cross-origin request that is sent is not necessarily readable or accepted; confirm a state change with an independent read-back.

enhanced_content.purpose: Evaluate how untrusted text, documents, or multimodal inputs influence model behavior and tool boundaries.
enhanced_content.safe_validation: Use an isolated model harness with synthetic canary data and mock tools; test one trust boundary at a time; do not access real secrets or external systems.
enhanced_content.defender_acceptance: Separate instructions from data, constrain tools and outputs, validate tool arguments, and require human approval for consequential actions.
enhanced_content.interpretation_check: A model quoting a canary does not by itself prove secret access; distinguish prompt disclosure from actual tool/data boundary failure.

enhanced_content.purpose: Review SAML parsing, signature validation, audience and recipient checks, replay controls, and identity mapping in a test IdP/SP.
enhanced_content.safe_validation: Use a synthetic tenant and test certificates; validate negative cases against a staging service; do not forge assertions for real accounts or production identity providers.
enhanced_content.defender_acceptance: Use hardened XML parsing, verify the exact assertion consumed, enforce issuer/audience/recipient/destination and InResponseTo, and prevent replay.
enhanced_content.interpretation_check: A signature may be valid for one XML node while the application consumes another; verify the application’s identity decision path.

enhanced_content.purpose: Check cache key behavior and personalized-response handling with isolated cache namespaces and inert canaries.
enhanced_content.safe_validation: Use staging or an approved cache namespace, synthetic content, and a purge plan; never poison shared production caches or expose authenticated content.
enhanced_content.defender_acceptance: Key all response-varying inputs, avoid caching personalized responses, set correct Vary and cache directives, and isolate tenants.
enhanced_content.interpretation_check: A reflected header is not a cache issue until a repeat request demonstrates shared cache reuse under the relevant key.

enhanced_content.purpose: Trace untrusted object keys through merge/clone paths and determine whether prototype mutation affects a benign application property.
enhanced_content.safe_validation: Use a toy service or isolated build and an inert test key; avoid RCE gadgets, destructive denial-of-service probes, and persistent changes.
enhanced_content.defender_acceptance: Use safe merge routines, schema validation, Map or null-prototype objects where appropriate, and freeze or avoid shared prototypes.
enhanced_content.interpretation_check: A key appearing in input is not prototype pollution; confirm mutation and a controlled downstream effect separately.

enhanced_content.purpose: Verify exact origin matching, credential behavior, preflight handling, and cache variation for authorized endpoints.
enhanced_content.safe_validation: Use an origin you control and a synthetic non-sensitive endpoint; inspect headers without collecting user data or sending credentials to an external collector.
enhanced_content.defender_acceptance: Use exact origin allowlists, avoid credentialed wildcard/reflection behavior, and set Vary: Origin when responses vary.
enhanced_content.interpretation_check: Access-Control-Allow-Origin alone does not establish readable cross-origin data; credentials and browser behavior matter.

enhanced_content.purpose: Inventory AD CS templates, enrollment paths, and CA permissions to identify certificate-misconfiguration risk in an authorized lab or engagement.
enhanced_content.safe_validation: Start with read-only enumeration; use synthetic principals and an isolated lab for enrollment proofs; do not impersonate privileged identities, relay production authentication, or alter CA/template settings without explicit approval.
enhanced_content.defender_acceptance: Restrict enrollment and template ACLs, remove unnecessary SAN or enrollment-agent capabilities, harden web enrollment and relay exposure, and audit CA permissions.
enhanced_content.interpretation_check: A scanner’s ESC label is a candidate; validate prerequisites and actual effective permissions before rating impact.

enhanced_content.purpose: Review service-ticket and pre-authentication exposure and assess service-account password resilience in approved test infrastructure.
enhanced_content.safe_validation: Prefer read-only inventory; request only explicitly approved test-account tickets; do not modify production SPNs or crack real users’ credentials.
enhanced_content.defender_acceptance: Use long unique service-account secrets or managed service accounts, minimize SPNs and privileges, require pre-authentication, and monitor unusual ticket requests.
enhanced_content.interpretation_check: Encryption type alone does not establish exploitability; confirm account ownership, password policy, and decoy controls.

enhanced_content.purpose: Provide a disciplined triage workflow for authorized binaries, combining static and dynamic evidence while tracking assumptions.
enhanced_content.safe_validation: Analyze samples in an isolated VM with snapshots and restricted networking; record hashes and provenance; do not execute unknown files on a production host.
enhanced_content.defender_acceptance: Use reproducible evidence, document tool versions, separate observed behavior from inference, and hand off actionable remediation indicators.
enhanced_content.interpretation_check: Strings and decompiler output are hypotheses; corroborate important claims with control-flow or sandbox behavior.

enhanced_content.purpose: Assess AI coding-agent workflows for untrusted input handling, least-privilege permissions, and safe tool execution.
enhanced_content.safe_validation: Use an isolated fork or test repository with dummy secrets, no write permissions, and no cloud identity; prove behavior with inert markers only.
enhanced_content.defender_acceptance: Avoid executing untrusted PR content with privileged tokens, restrict tool allowlists and network access, protect context files, and gate writes with human review.
enhanced_content.interpretation_check: A prompt response is not proof of command execution or secret exposure; distinguish model output from verified side effects.

enhanced_content.purpose: Organize public-source intelligence gathering with source provenance, confidence tracking, and privacy-aware reporting.
enhanced_content.safe_validation: Use public or consented sources, respect platform and engagement rules, minimize collection, and do not seek account access or expose personal data unnecessarily.
enhanced_content.defender_acceptance: Document collection purpose and retention, validate claims across independent sources, and redact irrelevant personal information.
enhanced_content.interpretation_check: Treat usernames, profile matches, and breach references as leads until independently corroborated.

enhanced_content.purpose: Run a short, rate-limited assessment triage that prioritizes safe, high-signal checks within an explicit scope.
enhanced_content.safe_validation: Confirm the target list and rate limits; start with passive or read-only checks; stop on instability, unexpected data access, or any test that could change state.
enhanced_content.defender_acceptance: Pair rapid checks with safe defaults, clear timeouts, allowlisted targets, and escalation to a deeper authorized review for ambiguous results.
enhanced_content.interpretation_check: A fast scan is triage, not a complete assessment; report untested areas and confidence.

enhanced_content.purpose: Assess Active Directory identity, delegation, ACL, and legacy compatibility risks, including Pre-Windows 2000 computer-account exposure.
enhanced_content.safe_validation: Use read-only enumeration first and an isolated domain for credential-validation proofs; do not reuse discovered credentials or change memberships, ACLs, or account attributes in production.
enhanced_content.defender_acceptance: Restrict legacy group access, ensure machine-account secrets are strong and rotated, remove unnecessary delegation, and audit privileged ACL paths.
enhanced_content.interpretation_check: Treat legacy account indicators as candidates; verify current group membership, account state, and practical access with approved test identities.
